'''Andrey Andreyevich Piontkovsky''' ({{langx|ru|Андрей Андреевич Пионтковский}}, born 30 June 1940) is a Russian-Georgian<ref>{{Cite web |last=Borkosvky |first=Antin |date=2020-04-29 |title=Андрей Пионтковский: Какие реформы вы собираетесь делать, президент Саакашвили, вместе с Ахметовым и Коломойским?! |trans-title=Andrei Piontkovsky: What reforms are you going to do, President Saakashvili, together with Akhmetov and Kolomoyskyi?! |url=https://ru.espreso.tv/article/2020/04/28/andrey_pyontkovskyy_kakye_reformy_vy_sobyraetes_delat_prezydent_saakashvyly_vmeste_s_akhmetovym_y_kolomoyskym |access-date=2024-08-30 |website=[[Espreso TV]] |language=ru |trans-quote=I am a citizen of Georgia, Saakashvili granted citizenship to me and some other Russian citizens by his decree in 2006}}</ref> [[scientist]] and political writer and analyst,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Klimina, Anna|title=The futility of the neoliberal policy of deliberate market construction and the promise of an institutionalist alternative: the case of Russia's authoritarian transition|journal=Journal of Economic Issues|date=2011|volume=45|issue=2|pages=411–420|doi=10.2753/JEI0021-3624450218|s2cid=154346707}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=AREA 17 |url=http://www.hudson.org/learn/index.cfm?fuseaction=staff_bio&eid=PiontAndr |title=Hudson Institute > About Hudson > Andrei A. Piontkovsky |publisher=Hudson.org |date=2014-05-13 |access-date=2014-05-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131026050431/https://www.hudson.org/learn/index.cfm?fuseaction=staff_bio&eid=PiontAndr |archive-date=2013-10-26 |url-status=dead }}</ref> a member of [[PEN International|International PEN Club]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Andrey Piontkovsky {{!}} Free Russia Foundation|work=Free Russia Foundation |date=11 July 2017 |url=https://www.4freerussia.org/andrey-piontkovsky/|access-date=2022-02-24|language=en-US}}</ref> He is a former member of the [[Russian Opposition Coordination Council]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Isaev, Gumer|title=Russia and Egypt: conflicts in the political elite and protest movements in 2011–2012|journal=Journal of Eurasian Studies|date=January 2014|volume=5|issue=1|pages=60–67|doi=10.1016/j.euras.2013.10.003|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Biography==
===Mathematics career===
He graduated from the Mathematics Department of [[Moscow State University]] and has published more than a hundred scientific papers on [[applied mathematics]]. Piontkovsky is a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]]. Early in his career he wrote on the terminal control problem,<ref name="mru1">{{cite news |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/at/v26/i7/p1137 |title=A. A. Piontkovsky, "On a Variant of the Terminal Control Problem", Avtomat. I Telemekh., 26:7 (1965), 1137–1144 }}</ref> and nonstationary nonlinear systems.<ref name="mru2">{{cite news |url=https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/at/y1970/i11/p179 |title=A. A. Piontkovsky, "Concerning Investigation of Stability of Nonstationary Nonlinear Systems", Avtomat. I Telemekh., 1970, no. 11, 179–181 }}</ref> Later papers were devoted to the mathematical modelling of strategic stability in the Cold War dual opponent system.<ref name="ap90">{{cite journal |doi=10.1177/019251219001100207 |title=Strategic Stability Analysis through Mathematical Modeling |date=1990 |last1=Gelovani |first1=V.A. |last2=Piontkovsky |first2=A.A. |last3=Skerokhodov |first3=A.P. |journal=International Political Science Review |volume=11 |issue=2 |pages=243–260 }}</ref>

===Polemical career===
In his article published on 11 January 2000 in [[Sovetskaya Rossiya]]<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Piontkovsky|first=Andrey|date=11 January 2000|title=Путинизм как высшая и заключительная стадия бандитского капитализма в России|trans-title=Putinism as highest and final stage of bandit capitalism in Russia|language=ru|magazine=Советская Россия|trans-magazine=Sovetskaya Rossiya|location=Moscow|issue=3}}</ref> and placed on the [[Yabloko]] website<ref>{{cite web|last=Piontkovsky|first=Andrey|date=11 January 2000|title=Путинизм как высшая и заключительная стадия бандитского капитализма в России|language=ru|publisher=[[Yabloko]]|url=https://www.yabloko.ru/Publ/Book/Fire/fire_002.html}}</ref> on the same day, was the first<ref>{{cite book|last1=Fedorov|first1=Valeriy|last2=Baskakova|first2=Yuliya|last3=Byzov|first3=Leontiy|last4=Chernozub|first4=Oleg|last5=Mamonov|first5=Mikhail|last6=Gavrilov|first6=Igor|last7=Vyadro|first7=Mikhail|date=2018|title=Выборы на фоне Крыма: электоральный цикл 2016–2018 гг. и перспективы политического транзита|trans-title=Elections against the backdrop of Crimea: election cycle 2016–2018 and perspectives of political transit|chapter="Путинизм" как социальный феномен и его ракурсы|trans-chapter="Putinism" as a social phenomenon and its aspects|editor-last=Fedorov|editor-first=Valeriy|language=ru|location=Moscow|publisher=[[Russian Public Opinion Research Center|ВЦИОМ]]|pages=587–602|isbn=978-5041523244}}</ref> to use the term "[[putinism]]" which he had defined as "the highest and final stage of bandit capitalism in Russia, the stage where, as one half-forgotten classic said, the bourgeoisie throws the flag of the democratic freedoms and the human rights overboard; and also as a war, "consolidation" of the nation on the ground of hatred against some ethnic group, attack on freedom of speech and information brainwashing, isolation from the outside world and further economic degradation". In the same article, Piontkovsky stated that putinism is the terminal shot to the head of Russia, and also he compared [[Boris Yeltsin|Yeltsin]] to [[Paul von Hindenburg|Hindenburg]] who in 1932 gave [[Adolf Hitler|Hitler]] power over Germany.

Piontkovsky was an executive director of the Strategic Studies Center (Moscow) think tank that has been closed since 2006. He contributed regularly to ''[[Novaya Gazeta]]'', ''[[The Moscow Times]]'', ''[[The Russia Journal]]'' and the online journals ''Grani.ru''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://graniru.org/|title=Грани.Ру: Главное|website=graniru.org}}</ref> and Transitions Online.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ehl |first=Martin |url=http://www.tol.cz |title=tol.cz |publisher=tol.cz |date= |access-date=2014-05-17}}</ref> He is also a regular political commentator for the [[BBC World Service]] and [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|Radio Liberty]] in Moscow. He was an outspoken critic of Putin's "managed" democracy in Russia and, as such, has described Russia as a "soft [[Totalitarianism|totalitarian]] regime"<ref>{{cite web|title=G8 members no longer have common goals, expert says|url=http://www.rferl.org/content/pressrelease/1105888.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081212012238/http://www.rferl.org/content/PressRelease/1105888.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 December 2008|publisher=[[Radio Liberty]]|date=31 July 2006}}</ref> and "hybrid fascism."<ref>{{cite news|author1=Lara, Philippe de|title=The dirty word "nationalism". Why absurd opinions on "Ukrainian nationalists" are so persistent, and need to be refuted again and again|url=http://ukrainianweek.com/Columns/50/150213|work=[[The Ukrainian Week]]|date=30 October 2015}}</ref>

Piontkovsky is the author of several books on the Putin presidency in Russia, including his most recent book, ''Another Look Into Putin's Soul.''<ref>{{cite web |author=AREA 17 |url=http://www.hudson.org/index.cfm?fuseaction=publication_details&id=4852 |title=Hudson Institute > Review of Andrei's Pionkovsky's Another Look Into Putin's Soul |publisher=Hudson.org |date=2014-05-13 |access-date=2014-05-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927230557/http://www.hudson.org/index.cfm?fuseaction=publication_details&id=4852 |archive-date=2007-09-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author=AREA 17 |url=http://www.hudson.org/index.cfm?fuseaction=publication_details&id=4852&pubType=HI_BookReviews |title=Hudson Institute > Review of Andrei's Pionkovsky's Another Look Into Putin's Soul |publisher=Hudson.org |date=2014-05-13 |access-date=2014-05-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120205054858/http://www.hudson.org/index.cfm?fuseaction=publication_details&id=4852&pubType=HI_BookReviews |archive-date=2012-02-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Piontkovsky is one of the 34 first signatories of the online anti-Putin manifesto "[[Putin Must Go]]", published on 10 March 2010. In his subsequent articles he has repeatedly stressed its importance and urged citizens to sign it.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://grani.ru/Politics/Russia/Cabinet/m.175922.html |title=Трон тронулся |publisher=Grani.ru |date=15 March 2010}}</ref>

On 26 June 2013, Piontkovsky commented the case of [[Edward Snowden]] by saying, "If [[Aleksey Pushkov|Pushkov]] dares to draw a parallel between Snowden and [[Soviet dissidents]], I must respond that none of them had anything to do with Soviet special services and none of them pledged not to betray state and departmental secrets."<ref>{{cite news|author=Loiko, Sergei|title=Russian lawmakers suggest U.S. is violating Snowden's human rights|url=https://www.latimes.com/world/la-xpm-2013-jun-26-la-fg-wn-russia-snowden-human-rights-20130626-story.html|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=26 June 2013}}</ref>

Piontkovsky compared the [[Crimean speech of Vladimir Putin]] in 2014 to [[Adolf Hitler|Hitler's]] speech on [[Occupation of Czechoslovakia (1938–1945)|Sudetenland]] in 1939. He described Putin as using "the same arguments and vision of history" and beyond that, that this speech played a key role in starting the [[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|war in Donbas]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://aru.tv/syuzhet/putin-sdelal-stavku-na-yadernyy-shantazh-andrey-piontkovskiy | title="Путин сделал ставку на ядерный шантаж" – Андрей Пионтковский | publisher=ARU.tv | date=2015-02-18 | access-date=2015-03-01 | author=Andrey Piontkovskiy | archive-date=27 February 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150227034525/http://aru.tv/syuzhet/putin-sdelal-stavku-na-yadernyy-shantazh-andrey-piontkovskiy | url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2016 he published an article "Бомба, готовая взорваться" ("A bomb that is ready to explode") about Russian-Chechen ethnic conflict.<ref>[http://zapretno.info/?p=1132  "Бомба, готовая взорваться" ("Bomb that is ready to explode")] by Piontkovsky.</ref> When the General Prosecutor Office found his article "extremist" and started criminal prosecution <ref>{{cite web|author=Piontkovsky, Andrey|title=Article "Бомба, готовая взорваться" in Russian.|url=http://echo.msk.ru/blog/piontkovsky_a/1699370-echo/|publisher=[[Echo of Moscow]]|date=23 January 2016}}</ref> Piontkovsky at last left Russia on 19 February 2016.<ref>{{cite web|author=Schreck, Carl|title=Russian analyst flees country, fearing persecution|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/russian-analyst-flees-fearing-prosecution/27562352.html|publisher=[[Radio Liberty]]|date=19 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Андрей Пионтковский покинул Россию, опасаясь преследования|trans-title=Andrey Piontkovsky fled Russia, fearing persecution|url=http://www.bbc.com/russian/news/2016/02/160219_piontkovsky_feigin_abroad|publisher=[[BBC Russian Service]]|language=ru|date=19 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Адвокат Пионтковского: любой человек может опасаться за свою жизнь|trans-title=Piontkovsky's lawyer: anyone can fear for his life|url=http://www.bbc.com/russian/society/2016/02/160219_mark_feigin_interview|publisher=[[BBC Russian Service]]|language=ru|date=19 February 2016}}</ref>

====2014 condemnation of fascism====
Piontkovsky adduces [[Igor Girkin]]'s name among those of like-minded persons and says, "The ''authentic high-principled Hitlerites'', ''true [[Aryan race|Aryans]]'' [[Aleksandr Dugin|Dugin]], [[Alexander Prokhanov|Prokhanov]], {{ill|Yegor Prosvirnin|ru|Просвирнин, Егор Александрович|lt=Prosvirnin}}, [[Yegor Kholmogorov|Kholmogorov]], [[Igor Girkin|Girkin]], [[Zakhar Prilepin|Prilepin]] are a marginalized minority in Russia."<ref name="Пионтковский1">{{cite web|author=Андрей Пионтковский|script-title=ru:На "Русском мире" держится пожизненная власть Путина|url=http://podrobnosti.ua/opinion/2014/10/27/999963.html|publisher=[[Podrobnosti.ua]]|date=27 October 2014|language=ru}}</ref><ref name="Пионтковский2">{{cite web|author=Андрей Пионтковский|script-title=ru:Военная доктрина "Русского Мира"|url=http://www.kasparov.ru/material.php?id=544C06FC3943D|publisher=[[Kasparov.ru]]|language=ru|date=26 October 2014}}</ref> Piontkovsky adds, "Putin has stolen the ideology of the Russian Reich from the domestic Hitlerites, he has preventively burned them down, using their help to do so, hundreds of their most active supporters in the furnace of the Ukrainian [[War in the Vendée|Vendée]]."<ref name="Пионтковский1"/><ref name="Пионтковский2"/> In his interview with [[Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty|Radio Liberty]], Piontkovsky says that maybe the meaning of the operation conducted by Putin is to reveal all these potential ''passionate leaders of social revolt'', send them to Ukraine and burn them in the furnace of the Ukrainian Vendée.<ref>{{cite news|author=Михаил Соколов|newspaper=Радио Свобода |script-title=ru:Крах проекта "Новороссия"?|url=http://www.svoboda.org/content/transcript/25450590.html|publisher=[[Radio Liberty]]|language=ru|date=9 July 2014}}</ref>

===Exile in America===
In an interview published on 11 February 2022 Piontkovsky argues that the ideology of [[Rashism]] is in many ways similar to German fascism ([[Nazism]]),<ref>{{Citation |title=Що переможе: здоровий глузд чи імперські амбіції? Андрій Піонтковський. | date=11 February 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wucOzeeCq8A |language=en |access-date=2022-02-26}}</ref> while in an interview published on 11 August 2021 he opines that the speeches and policies of Putin are similar to the ideas of Hitler.<ref>{{Citation |title="Путинский режим — постмодернистский фашизм" |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3erAJI8nFo |language=en |publisher=RFE/RL |date=2021-09-11}}</ref>

Piontkovsky has written extensively on political affairs for the [[Jamestown Foundation]],<ref name="jorg1">{{cite news |url=https://jamestown.org/analyst/andrei-piontkovsky/ |title=Andrei Piontkovsky }}</ref> the [[Kyiv Post]],<ref name="kpost1">{{cite news |url=https://www.kyivpost.com/authors/820 |title=Andrei Piontkovsky, Author at the Kyiv Post }}</ref> and [[Project Syndicate]].<ref name="ps1">{{cite news |url=https://www.project-syndicate.org/columnist/andrei-piontkovsky |title=Andrei Piontkovsky }}</ref> His byline includes mention that he is a visiting fellow at the [[Hudson Institute]].<ref name=ps1/>
